summary: Ready-to-use Python OCR that reads text from images in 80+ languages, including Latin, Chinese, Arabic, Devanagari and Cyrillic scripts.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: EasyOCR is a Python library that finds and reads text in images. You create a Reader with the languages you need and call readtext on an image file, an OpenCV array, bytes or an image URL. It returns each piece of text with its bounding box and a confidence score, and it also has a command-line tool.
sixtySeconds.problem: Pulling text from photos, screenshots and scans in many languages usually needs complex setup. EasyOCR works in a few lines and downloads the language models it needs automatically.
whoFor: Python developers extracting text from images
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a simple API with wide language coverage that runs on GPU or CPU.
requirements: PyTorch (on Windows, install torch and torchvision first)

overview: Install from PyPI with pip install easyocr. On Windows, install torch and torchvision first from pytorch.org with the right CUDA version. A Dockerfile is also provided.
Create a Reader with a list of languages (English works with every language), then call readtext. Model weights download automatically on first use, or you can place them in ~/.EasyOCR/model.
Without a GPU, pass gpu=False to run on the CPU. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.
limitations: Not all languages can be combined in one Reader
